sentence_level_patterns.average_sentence_length: Action-line average is 6.7 words per line across 991 lines (6013 words total), with most lines landing in the 1-5 word range and very few exceeding 18 words.
sentence_level_patterns.cadence_variation: Strong alternation between ultra-short isolate beats and short/medium clarifying lines; the dominant pulse is fragment cluster -> isolated beat -> short clarification -> image/status close.
sentence_level_patterns.clause_structure_preference: Prefers fragments, short declaratives, and corrective negation chains over subordinated clauses; when longer lines appear, they usually carry technical clarification or a single emotional turn.
sentence_level_patterns.punctuation_habits: Heavy period use, light comma use, zero semicolons and zero exclamation marks across the full source; question marks are sparse and mostly in dialogue; ellipses are rare and tied to broken V.O.; em-dashes appear only a handful of times and are not a house rhythm.

scene_transition_compression_protocol.transition_guidance: End scenes on a concrete image, bodily status, or tiny beat. Do not summarize what the scene meant. Let the last line feel like residue: an object, a condition, a motion, or a one-word verdict.

element_rules.prose_translation_rule: Translate into second-person present-tense narration while preserving fragment density, clipped syntax, and sensory priority. Do not expand into novelistic description.
Convert to one brief establishing sentence or a white-space break. Keep location/time orientation minimal and functional.
Render as a hard paragraph or scene break. Do not bridge with 'meanwhile' or explanatory connective tissue.
Translate into a minimal delivery tag or adjacent physical cue, e.g. 'she says, low.' Never turn it into narrator psychology.
Use minimal attribution. 'says' or no tag if clear. Preserve the speaker's compression and ceiling.
Translate sparingly into emphasis through sentence isolation, not exclamation. System text may remain in caps when diegetic.
Replace with a physical pause or object interaction. Never write 'there is a moment of silence.'

voice_anchor.source: Nora exits the Citadel and realizes Mirror assets are deploying through reflections.
voice_anchor.techniques: reflection-to-agent metamorphosis; HUD intrusion syntax; fragment pressure stacking
voice_anchor.prose: You step into rain and daylight and think, for one second, that the world is still the world. Then the doors seal behind you and the cold chime hits. NONCOMPLIANT. LICENSE SUSPENDED. RESOURCES FROZEN. The text hangs in your vision too long. ENFORCEMENT ACTIVE. You look up. A man sits on a bench across the plaza, eyes closed, smiling at nothing. At his feet, the puddle moves first. Chrome slides across the reflection. The face simplifies. It peels itself out of the water and stands on the concrete looking straight at you. Down the plaza, another reflection is already out. Then another. Three bodies. Suit, skin, geometry. Off by a degree. You turn. They accelerate.

voice_anchor.source: Nora destroys the surveillance pillar while Agents close in through the alley.
voice_anchor.techniques: impact verb emphasis; clipped kinetic sequencing; glitch-spread imagery
voice_anchor.prose: You hit the pillar with your thumb still on the forged tether and the surface answers wrong. Not metal. Not stone. Static. The skin of it STUTTERS. Lines of glitch spread fast under your hand, racing through the housing, up the feed spine, across the alley walls. The nearest Agent jerks mid-step. Pixelates. Keeps coming. You wrench the tether harder. The pillar fractures outward. Light spits through the seams. Then the node goes. A hard pop. Spray of molten circuitry. The alley flashes white-blue and the Agents break with it, bodies losing edge, then structure, then purpose. One drops to a knee. One folds at the waist. One comes apart into chrome dust and rain. You do not wait to watch the rest. You run.

voice_anchor.source: Post-surgery recovery when Nora realizes Eli is gone from the hardware.
voice_anchor.techniques: fragment laddering; tactile absence; withheld emotional naming
voice_anchor.prose: You sit against the wall with the lens at your chest and the new port cooling clean at the base of your skull. The data survived. The mission survived. What lived in the hardware did not. You touch the surgical ridge and wait for the old warmth to answer. Nothing. Not pain. Absence. The tether carries him across the alcove with a clarity that should feel like relief. His breathing comes through the channel sharp and direct, the cleanest sound you have ever heard. The loneliest. When you say Eli's name now, it is only a word. No pressure under it. No presence shaping the syllables from inside your head. The room inside your skull is still there. Same walls. Nothing inside.

voice_anchor.source: Nora walks through the city after the filters are gone.
voice_anchor.techniques: nominal fragment chaining; concrete moral observation; real-vs-managed contrast
voice_anchor.prose: You walk through a city that no longer corrects itself for you. The billboards are dark. Some stripped for parts. Some painted over. Murals in their place. Crude. Human. The memorial kiosks stand empty, their ports dead, and someone has left real flowers in one. Wilting already. You keep your scar visible. You do not cover it. A man sits alone with a phone in his hand, looking at a photograph, his mouth tight. He sits with it. His grief is his. In the park, the false garden is gone. Real flowers grow there now, uneven, patchy, stubborn. A woman kneels in the dirt with black soil on her fingers. She looks up. Nods once. Nothing else. You nod back and keep moving.

voice_anchor.source: Nora and Jace meet under the junction beacon and recognize each other through the tether.
voice_anchor.techniques: dry pressure dialogue; object-based characterization; static-charged proximity
voice_anchor.prose: You find him under the beacon in rain needling through neon fog, and the first thing he gives you is not trust but a correction. Not chrome. Ugly. He keeps his palms up. You read the favor in his stance, the wrong shine at one iris, the shape hidden under his jacket and held too close to be casual. He sees the cord at your sternum and the weight hanging there. "Yours," you say. "Yours," he says back. That is how the recognition lands. Not with relief. With inventory. The tether reacts before either of you moves away. Static crawls through your teeth. Your HUD flares. He blinks hard. "Proximity makes it worse," he says. Neither of you steps back.

voice_anchor.source: Nora refuses the Mirror's offer in the decode chamber.
voice_anchor.techniques: negation calibration; object as grief totem; technical-emotional braid
voice_anchor.prose: You hold the lens against your chest and feel the port answer with a warmth you know too well. It is almost his voice. Not his face. Not him. Just the cadence close enough to tighten everything under your ribs. The system offers terms in the language of mercy: no more passes, no more damage, every coordinate handed over clean. The cruel part is that it knows why the offer works. You kept the residue because it was the last place he lived. You let the corruption stay because erasing it felt too much like burying him twice. The pull in your hand is grief, not trust. You count once. Twice. Then you say no and stand, and the warmth drains out of the hardware in stages.

voice_anchor.source: Nora rejects the final Eli reconstruction during collapse.
voice_anchor.techniques: forensic mismatch detection; negation correction cadence; intimate-detail proof
voice_anchor.prose: You stop because the voice comes through the clean channel in the one place you never sealed. It offers him back in pieces so exact they should work: the apartment, the lens before the crack, his body standing where memory left it. Then the error lands. The camera is in the wrong hand. The sentence is too finished. The copy knows his face and voice and prints, but it does not know mornings. It does not know the click through the wall before coffee. You feel the break in yourself and hold it there. No clean versions. No mercy rewrites. The real thing was damaged, unfinished, yours. The image fails under that truth. The room gives way. The dying architecture starts moving again, and you run.

voice_anchor.source: Final apartment scene with Nora and Jace in the rain.
voice_anchor.techniques: parallel vow dialogue; stillness as intimacy; object-anchor close
voice_anchor.prose: You come back at evening, hang the pendant and lens on the hook, and let the cord swing once before it goes still. He is on the floor against the wall, recorder beside him, chrome arm across his knee, the mug empty in his hand. You sit down next to him. The wall is cold behind you. Your shoulders touch. Rain starts at the window, soft at first, then steady enough to fill the room. He turns his head toward you, the last light catching the chrome side of his face. "If you forget," he says. "I will remind you." "If you drift." "I will pull." Neither of you reaches. You do not need to. You are already close enough. When the room goes dark, he is still there. Still here.

anchor_card: Use short fragments freely. Let many sentences land at 1-5 words.
Break pressure with isolated one-word or two-word beats.
Prefer periods over commas. Never use semicolons.
Do not open sentences with -ing forms unless there is no cleaner option.
Render emotion through body change, object contact, or system intrusion before naming it.
Use 'Not X. Y.' corrections sparingly but decisively when refining perception or truth.
Keep dialogue short. Nora max 13 words, Jace max 11, Riven max 12, Ilya max 12, Mirror max 13.
End scenes on an image, status condition, action beat, or tiny verdict. Never on explanation.
Use ALL CAPS only for diegetic system text, object reveals, entities, or rare impact emphasis.
Do not use camera-direction terms like WE SEE, CLOSE ON, ANGLE ON, or PAN.
Let charged objects carry grief: lens, recorder, pendant, photograph, cord.
runtime_self_check: SEARCH for semicolons, exclamation marks, and camera-direction terms like WE SEE, CLOSE ON, ANGLE ON, PAN. Delete every one and restructure.
SEARCH for cognitive lead-ins and interior-summary phrasing such as realized, noticed, became aware, found yourself, felt that, remembered that. Delete them and render the experience directly.

SEARCH for banned molds and generic substitutes: neon-poetry atmosphere, therapeutic grief language, 'it felt fake,' long lore explanation, overt romantic declaration. Replace with concrete object, body, or system detail.
SCAN the last three sentence openers. If three consecutive open the same way, vary one with a fragment, negation, or object-first line.
SCAN sentence lengths. If multiple medium or long sentences run in sequence, cut them back into fragments and short clarifiers.
SCAN dialogue. If any character exceeds their speech ceiling, compress. If the line sounds chatty, witty, or explanatory, compress again.

GLANCE at the nearest voice anchor exemplar. If the passage reads smoother, more lyrical, more explanatory, or less externalized than the anchor, rewrite toward harder stops, object focus, and scene-end residue.

quantitative_checks: Generate 8-12 sample passages, including cold open, branch outcomes, freeform replies, and one 600+ word continuous sample.
Check fragment distribution against source band: target 58-62% of sentences at 5 words or fewer; flag if below 54% or above 66%.
Check sentence-length bucket distribution against source ranges for 1-3w, 4-5w, 6-8w, 9-12w, 13-18w, 19-25w, and 26+w.
Check ABSOLUTE punctuation bans: semicolons must be zero; exclamation marks must be zero.
Check em-dash frequency stays near-zero and never becomes a default interruption device.
Check period-to-comma ratio remains within 2.2:1 to 3.4:1.
Check -ing sentence openings remain at or below 1% of sentence starts.
Check dialogue ceilings per character: Nora <=13, Jace <=11, Riven <=12, Ilya <=12, Mirror <=13.
Check scene endings in samples: at least 80% should land on image, status, action, or beat rather than explanation.
Check signature-technique drift: negation calibration, object grief tether, and micro-beat isolation should appear regularly but not every paragraph.
Check rhythm-change frequency in long samples; if same-length sentence runs dominate, flag for smoothing drift.
Check ALL CAPS usage: only diegetic system text, object/entity reveal, or rare impact emphasis.
judgment_checks: Blind attribution test: compare a generated sample against a real source passage. If a familiar reader can instantly spot the generated one as generic prose, fail.
Comparative exclusion test: ensure no sample reads more like Alex Garland, Tony Gilroy, or Villeneuve/Heisserer than this writer.
Character differentiation swap test: swap Nora, Jace, Riven, and Ilya lines in dialogue-bearing samples. If the swap still reads plausible, fail.
Emotional rendering test: grief, fear, and intimacy must arrive through body, object, and omission rather than named explanation.
Scene-close residue test: final lines should linger as afterimage or status, not thesis.
build_time_qa_protocol.decay_test_procedure: Generate one continuous 600+ word sample. Compare the first 200 words to the last 200 words for sentence length, fragment density, punctuation ratio, dialogue compression, and explanatory drift. If the tail has fewer fragments, more commas, more abstract interpretation, smoother connective tissue, or longer speeches than the head, decay is occurring. Repair upstream by strengthening the voice anchor, sharpening the anchor card, and increasing re-anchoring cadence.

voice_decay_prevention_protocol.re_anchoring_trigger: Every 300-400 words of generated prose, or immediately after any long dialogue exchange or branch-resolution passage.
passage_level_enforcement_checks: At least one fragment or isolate beat near major emotional turns.
Scene endings land on image, status, action, or beat.
drift_detection_metrics: Fragment rate dropping below source band.
Comma density rising while period density falls.
